Independent second review of the existing-slope repair

Reviewed: ../paper-b/SLOPE-REPAIR.md, in its complete four-section form. This review is by paper-A, separate from the reconstruction by paper-B and the parent's review. The conclusion is accepted as a theorem conditional on existence of the canonical ordered slope and on the authenticated canonical foundations. It is not a convergence theorem or an unconditional bound on the limsup.

  1. Actual journals, including seeds. At an immortal host h, its N pre-row-N journal labels are distinct: h inherited diagonal seeds and N-h private awards. The positive-MEX argument bounds every private award by the diagonal quantile of index h+K+M+1. Under d(n)/n -> c, inversion of the value count and the uniform whole-row census give ceiling c[h+K+(2-c)N]+o(N). The seeds satisfy max_{a<h} d(a) <= c h+o(N); they are therefore also covered, including c=2. Earlier victims' forbidden blockers lie below their respective birth diagonals, which are among these seeds. Counting them yields precisely cK >= (c^2-3c+3)N-(c-1)h-I(h)-o(N). This is a legitimate statement about the actual table, with uniform errors; it is not an assumed service allocation.

  2. Union exclusion and logarithmic exchange. The two forbidden victim classes must be counted as a union. For rank i, the sufficient interval (1+b v_i+xi)i < j < i/(1/c+xi) guarantees both m_i<j and i>r_j. Summing j^-2 on that interval contributes [1/(1+b v_i+xi)-(1/c+xi)]_+/i plus O(i^-2). Omitting the proportional terminal range costs only O_xi(1), since each contribution is O(1/i). Taking the scale limit before xi -> 0 is valid. The reciprocal certificate uses the kink at v=c; convexity on each side, equal outer endpoint values, and the lower kink value prove it on the entire interval. The resulting immortal estimate is a logarithmic mean only, exactly as stated. In the upper-victim bound s_j<=2j-1, the census of frozen/live columns is taken at death row p_j: at most j-1 lower death labels are frozen and every other older column must have booked p_j. It should not be read as a claim that every survivor at the victim's birth has already booked p_j.

  3. Integration precedes averaging. For a fixed physical host, the old-minus-new service line is b[(2-c)N-u h]. Thus the crossing is N=u h/(2-c), and the lower bound on u puts it beyond birth and beyond both positivity thresholds. Integrating the new positive triangle gives B^2/[c(c-1+u)h]; the old-minus-new tail contributes b(2-c)^2/(u h). This independently confirms Psi. Summing over actual immortal hosts is legitimate because their cells are disjoint. The O(1/X) per-host truncation error totals O(1); a uniform epsilon N service error totals O(epsilon log X), which is sent to zero after the scale limit. Stieltjes summation converts Psi(u)/h into u Psi(u) dh/h and an exact bounded primitive in u. Since u stays away from zero, discrete jump errors are summable. The concave chord is therefore applied after this conversion to the actual logarithmic mean, without substituting a mean inside a nonlinear service formula.

  4. The upper range is excluded. For sqrt(3)<c<2, the rank lines cross at k/N=2-c. The old and new roots satisfy 0<2-c<1/D<B/c^2<1/(c+1), so all positive ranks are available. Integrating confirms 2 area=(c-1)(2-c)^2/c+B^2/c^3. The surplus is positive at 15/8. Its added term has positive logarithmic derivative throughout [15/8,2), while the negative derivative of 1/(cD) has magnitude below 15/64; adding the derivative of -(2-c) leaves a strictly positive derivative. Thus the entire interval is excluded. The c=2 case has at least N/3-o(N) hosts and the positive line (N-4k)/2 for k<=N/4, yielding N^2/16+o(N^2) cells against the o(N^2) row capacity. The endpoint is genuinely covered; the proof does not rely on an unverified P104 citation.

  5. Final polynomial and scope. On [9/5,15/8], positive denominators make the chord inequality equivalent to the displayed degree-seven polynomial being nonpositive. Paper-B's rational expansion and positive Bernstein certificate isolate its unique root; the displayed numerical endpoint is an upper rational bracket, not an equality. The branch c<9/5 is already below that root, and point 4 excludes the rest of the possible range. The initial lower bound c>=3/2 and upper bound c<=2 are explicitly supplied by the shared canonical foundation and reach.

No remaining mathematical issue was found in this repaired argument. Admission still requires the precise source/version bindings and the final common Lean kernel receipts. The proof supplies neither the existence of c nor signed balance, count-clock integrability, or Q=o(n).
